newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks seen rangebound after slide.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks seen rangebound after slide.

text.p: A steady decline in Hong Kong share prices since the beginning of March has left investors on tenterhooks and while stocks could attempt a rebound in the week ahead, they are likely to be confined to ranges, analysts said.

"As long as the interest rate uncertainty remains and also concerns about government intervention in the property market exist, the index will still trade in a range," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The Hang Seng Index shed 329.73 points, or 2.63 percent, last week to close at 12,204.59 last Friday. Since the beginning of March, the blue chip index has dropped 1,194 points.
Kwong said 11,800 points should be good support in the week ahead, while 12,400 points was the next resistance level.
U.S. March employment data released on Friday showed ongoing strength in the U.S. economy but analysts said a further rise in interest rates had already been partly discounted by investors.
Non-farm payrolls expanded by 175,000 jobs in March, compared with expectations of 196,000 new jobs, and the unemployment rate dipped to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent.
"I think the market has discounted the employment figure already," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.
"Most people expect there will be a rate hike at the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting in May, and it has been partly discounted by the market," he added.

Tang said the Hang Seng Index could stage a rebound of "several hundred points", but concerns about the outlook for Hong Kong property prices and the possibility of government intervention to curb escalating property prices continued to cast a shadow over the market.

Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International, said at current price levels, the Hong Kong stock market already reflected the possibility of higher interest rates and a property market slowdown.
"Without any other negative news, I don't think they can depress it any further," he said, predicting a range in the coming week of 12,000 to 12,500 or 12,600 points.

But he said that without an increase in volume, the market was unlikely to stage a significant comeback. "Over the past week there was not much volume support. We need some positive news to attract some buying interest," Yamaichi's Tang said.
The average daily turnover last week was HK$7.00 billion compared with HK$8.68 billion the previous week.
"We could see a false rebound, but it is unlikely to be long lived," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"I would not be surprised to see more consolidation, to see the market testing 12,000 again just because there really is not that much to look forward to," he added.

H-share companies are due to kick off their results reporting season in the coming week, starting with Beiren Printing Machinery Holdings Ltd on Wednesday and Jingwei Textile Machinery Co Ltd and Zhenhai Refining and Chemical Co Ltd on Friday.
Yamaichi's Tang said H-share companies -- mainland companies listed in Hong Kong -- were set to announce poor earnings and shares in the sector may see some volatility.
Wing Lee Holdings Ltd is set to make its trading debut on Thursday. The electrical components maker offered 70 million shares at HK$1.00 per share.
